author: Kamikaze
content: Hey Harsh, I have had pretty similar incidents in my life. When I was born, my dad had a free moving parrot named Parry whom he saved from a boy who stole him from his nest. I was a new born baby and the parrot used to sit on my forehead and sometimes used to sleep in our room. Unfortunately one day a visiting relative turned on the fan when he was there and he was hit by its blades. Years later, when I was in 5th/6th, my dad again rescued 3 tiny parrots from a bird seller. We kept them and as with you, even we had to release them. My dad released the seemingly fittest of them and then the other the other day. Two days later, my dad was on the terrace and he whistled, and lo behold.....both of them came flying back to him. We later released the 3rd one also and then all three started coming back to us. We had a photo session and were in talks with Discovery to cover the thing but unfortunately, we had to leave the town for a month and when we returned, they had migrated to some other place. I still remember Diego,Platinee and Boom boom - when I used to come back from school, they would swoop down from the peepul tree and one would sit on left, one on right and the third on my head. After that we had a bulbul with us in 10th grade. Your post brought back all those childhood memories. :)

author: Kamikaze
content: And the hostility to outsiders- that I have heard was with Parry too - my dad didn't allow the other 3 in the house for the fear of what happened with Parry happening to them. Parry used to aim straight for any stranger's foot and would bite horribly is not shooed away in time. Btw what is your parrot's name?
